'''Rupert Huber''' (born 1973, in [[Traunstein]])<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-physik.de/nachrichten/leibniz-preis-von-ultraschnellen-phaenomenen-und-nanomagnetismus|title=Leibniz-Preis: Von ultraschnellen Phänomenen und Nanomagnetismus &#124; pro-physik.de|website=www.pro-physik.de}}</ref> is a German physicist and university professor.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-regensburg.de/pressearchiv/pressemitteilung/347751.html|title=Newsmeldung – Universität Regensburg|website=www.uni-regensburg.de}}</ref> Huber is known for his research in terahertz technology and [[semiconductor]] physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.physik.uni-regensburg.de/forschung/huber/home.html|title=Lehrstuhl Huber|website=www.physik.uni-regensburg.de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dfg.de/gefoerderte_projekte/wissenschaftliche_preise/leibniz-preis/2019/huber/index.jsp|title=DFG – Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft – Prof. Dr. Rupert Huber – Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz-Preisträger 2019|website=www.dfg.de}}</ref>

==Career==

Huber attended the [[Technical University of Munich]] where he majored in physics. He was awarded a PhD in 2003 from [[University of California, Berkeley]]. In 2010 he became a professor at the [[University of Regensburg]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dfg.de/en/funded_projects/prizewinners/leibniz_prize/2019/huber/index.jsp|title=DFG, German Research Foundation – Prof. Dr. Rupert Huber|website=www.dfg.de}}</ref>

He is particularly well known for his research on [[Terahertz radiation|terahertz]] physics at the interface between optics and electronics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz-Preisträger 2019: Rupert Huber |url=https://www.dfg.de/gefoerderte_projekte/wissenschaftliche_preise/leibniz-preis/2019/index.jsp#huber |access-date=2023-11-11 |website=dfg.de |language=de}}</ref> In the framework of so-called lightwave electronics, his research group uses the carrier field of light as an ultrafast electrical bias.<ref name=":2">{{cite web |author=Alexander Schlaak |date=2014-01-20 |title=Pressemitteilung: Was Elektronen zum Zittern bringt |url=https://www.uni-regensburg.de/pressearchiv/pressemitteilung/347751.html ==Awards==
* 2004: Feodor Lynen Research Fellowship from the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation
* 2007: Emmy-Noether grant and DFG junior research group
* 2008: European THz Young Investigator Award from the European Optical Society
* 2009: Rudolf Kaiser Prize of the Donors' Association for German Science
* 2012: ERC Starting Grant (European Research Council)  
* 2016: Prize for good teaching at the state universities in Bavaria 
* 2019: [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]]<ref name="auto"/>
* 2019: Appointment as Fellow of the Optical Society of America (OSA)
